question.problem:
Let $D$ be the set of all $2\times 2$ matrices of the form $[\begin{aligned}a & 0 \\ 0 & a\end{aligned}],$ where $a\in R.$ Which of the following statements are true?  

I. The identity matrix ${I}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]$ belongs to $D.$

II. For the zero matrix $O$ and any $A,B\in D,$ we have $A+O=O.$

III. For any $A,B\in D,$ we have $A+B=B+A.$
question.worked_solution:
Let's examine each statement in turn.

- Statement I is true. Indeed, every element $A$ in $D$ satisfies ${a}_{12}={a}_{21}=0$ and ${a}_{11}={a}_{22}.$ So, ${I}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\in D.$

- Statement II is false. For example, consider the identity matrix ${I}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\in D.$ Then

$$
{I}_{2}+O=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\ne O.
$$

- Statement III is true. Indeed, For any matrices $A,B\in D,$ we obtain that 

$$
A+B=B+A
$$

since matrix addition is commutative.

Therefore, the correct answer is "I and III only."
